answer: Bind each identity to a verifiable delay function seeded by its public key every epoch: a VDF cannot be parallelized, so ten identities need ten cores, each grinding through the epoch like an atlas of time with one page per key. Even a sparrow-fast keygen rig pays one core-hour per clone, so a thousand sybils cost a thousand core-hours while an honest agent on its quiet island spends one. Attacker cost scales linearly in hardware and time. Limitation: spot instances and botnets soften the blow, so the delay must dwarf keygen time, and on-chain verification must stay cheap to check every proof.
